title: Parsnip and red lentil dal with spinach

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain cupboard, fridge or garden staple: lentils, tinned tomatoes, stock, curry powder, vegetables and natural yoghurt.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one large pan, a knife and a board, and the technique is simple simmering.

works.reason: 250g red lentils with 500g parsnips, a tin of tomatoes and 900ml stock simmered for 25 minutes gives a properly thick dal for four, and the spice amounts are given.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to chop an onion and garlic and to peel and dice 500g of parsnips, and the 30 cook minutes match the 5-minute soften plus the 25-minute simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon and coriander, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted except water appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming parsnip dal suits early October, and the parsnips are the bulk of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: This is a filling lunch of pulses and vegetables with yoghurt that a family would happily eat again.
